Subject: ArborX dedicated sizing scenario and burst runway request

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the chat earlier. To produce a recommended Dedicated pool and burst runway we need a few concrete inputs from your side so our sizing model (attached) can return an apples-to-apples recommendation. When you get a sec can you confirm the following workload assumptions for the primary production model you intend to serve?

- Typical prompt+response token mix (median): ~prompt 80 tokens / response 320 tokens?
- Peak 95th percentile concurrent requests during US business hours (TPS): is the ~300 tps figure you mentioned above peak or sustained for the hour?
- SLOs: 95th percentile generation latency target (single-stream) — you mentioned ~250 ms target; confirm.
- Preferred model family to serve (open variants OK) and whether you’ll allow int8/4 quantized runtime for cost tradeoffs.

I attached an initial workbook with three stress scenarios (baseline, 2x peak, burst 5x) and a runbook draft. If you confirm the bullets, Marissa will run a desk-sizing pass and Karthik will propose a resilient slab layout (primary + burst buffer + fallback).

Next steps we propose: you confirm numbers by end of day Wed (8/4) -> Redwood returns a pooled sizing proposal and cost delta vs hosted in 48 hours -> we schedule a 30-min walkthrough.

Thanks,

Hi Stephanie —

Thanks — confirming details below so you have exact inputs for the workbook. I pasted our telemetry slices:

- Typical prompt+response: median prompt 65 tokens, median response 420 tokens, 99th response occasionally up to 1,100 tokens (long-form analysis).
- Requests: baseline daytime sustained ~120 tps; expected busy-window peak (marketing/feature events) ~480 tps sustained for 10–30 minutes; extreme bursts observed up to ~1,800 tps for short spikes (1–3 minutes).
- SLO: 95p end-to-end generation latency target 300 ms; business will accept 500 ms for fallback model in extreme bursts.
- Model: Preference to run an open 70B architecture (quant-friendly) for primary; fallback to a smaller 13B for burst/failover. Quantization: procurement is open to int8 but we need to understand quality delta.
- Data retention/encryption: standard enterprise controls, SOC-2 evidence requested later.

Procurement will need a rough committed GPU count and burst buffer sizing for the term sheet. Hope this helps — happy to hop on a call if useful.

Cheers,
Liam

Stephanie / team —

I ran the initial desk-sizing against Liam's numbers and the attached workbook has the math. Summary (high level):

- Assumptions used: 70B int8-equivalent throughput baseline: ~45 tokens/sec per H100 v2 replica at 512 context when serving single-stream low-latency; 13B fallback ~220 tokens/sec per H100 replica. (See sheet 'perf_basis')
- Baseline sustained 120 tps (median payload ~485 tokens total) -> baseline steady-state demand ~58k tokens/sec (calculated as tps * avg tokens). With batching and prefix caching we assumed effective per-GPU throughput improves ~1.6x for steady-state workloads.
- Peak busy-window 480 tps sustained (30m): sizing implies needing a pool capable of ~230k tokens/sec to avoid violating 300 ms SLO under steady busy-window; that's roughly 6–8 H100 replicas in the primary slab (with our batching/caching assumptions).
- Burst spikes (~1,800 tps for 1–3min): recommend a burst buffer sized to absorb ~750k tokens in that window. Practically we model this as a combination of short-lived rented burst capacity (cloud spot or burst pool) + fast fallback to 13B replicas that increase effective throughput 3–4x per GPU for bursts.
- Headroom recommendation: target 30% operational headroom above busy-window steady requirements (to cover degradation, in-flight prefix rebuilds, and deployment churn).

Attached: arborx_sizing_model.xlsx with scenario tabs and conservative latency curves. I've flagged sensitivity rows where quantization yields quality risk; those need Product/ML signoff.

Marissa

Thanks Marissa — good work. A few concrete ops-level recommendations to include in the proposal:

1) Slab layout suggestion (primary + burst + fallback):
   - Primary slab: 8 x H100 replicas (dedicated pool), pinned for steady throughput.
   - Burst buffer: 4 x H100 pre-warmed burst nodes (auto-scale to 12 x H100 via spot/ephemeral for 2–5 minute windows).
   - Fallback slab: 6 x H100 running 13B runtime (or mixed A100s if client prefers cost-effective legacy hardware).

2) Routing policy: route by latency SLO. If system detects sustained 95p > 350 ms, route new sessions to fallback 13B until primary recovers. Keep short-circuit thresholds conservative to avoid oscillation.

3) Quantization policy: enable int8 on up to 60% of inference pool as an opt-in path; surface quality regressions via Redwood Optimize evaluation hooks. If client tests show >4% quality degradation on critical prompts, fall back to full-precision nodes.

4) Observability: add 1-min token-level telemetry, per-route 95/99 latency, and a synthetic prompt set to detect quality regressions post-deploy.

5) Cost and deal impact: estimate committed 8 H100 dedicated slab + baseline bursted ephemeral = 30–35% lower cost vs equivalent hosted peak while giving predictable latency; exact numbers in the workbook.

I'll draft the technical appendix for the term sheet describing fallback thresholds and autoscale cooldown windows.

-Karthik

Liam / team —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Summary of what we will include in the formal proposal (deliverable by Tue EOD 8/10):

- Dedicated proposal: 8 x H100 primary slab (pinned), 4 x H100 pre-warmed burst buffer + autoscale to 12 via ephemeral instances for short spikes, fallback pool of 6 x H100 equivalent running 13B for degraded-mode routing.
- Operational headroom: 30% above busy-window to cover churn and degraded nodes.
- Latency SLO mapping: 95p target 300 ms on primary; fallback target 95p <= 500 ms. Automatic routing rules and cooldowns documented in appendix.
- Cost delta: committed slab + burst buffer expected to lower peak unit cost vs hosted while giving SLA-level predictability (detailed line items in workbook).
- Action items for ArborX: review the attached workbook, run quality checks on int8 sample set (we can run an eval with Redwood Optimize), and confirm procurement appetite for a 12-month commit or a 6-month pilot.

If you approve, Procurement (cc'd) can start the term-sheet path and we'll attach the technical appendix. Happy to schedule a 30-minute walkthrough of the workbook Thursday or Friday — which day works best?
